main.title: Martin Luther King Jr. wins the Nobel Peace Prize
main.subtitle: Nonviolence on the world stage
main.summary: The Nobel Peace Prize announced on 14 October 1964 recognized King’s nonviolent struggle for civil rights.

cards.heading: Nonviolence on the world stage
cards.text: Martin Luther King Jr. was named the Nobel Peace Prize laureate on October 14, 1964, for his nonviolent struggle for African American civil rights. At thirty-five, he was then the youngest recipient. The award brought international recognition to a movement built through marches, boycotts and resistance to segregation. King accepted it in Oslo on December 10, describing the honour as recognition of that wider movement. The award came in the year the United States passed the Civil Rights Act.

main.title: Dune
main.summary: Frank Herbert's Dune appeared in 1965 after publication in serial form.

cards.heading: Dune
cards.text: Frank Herbert's Dune appeared in 1965 after publication in serial form. It follows Paul Atreides as his family accepts control of Arrakis, a desert planet whose importance rests on spice. The substance extends life, enhances mental abilities and makes interstellar navigation possible, giving control of its only source enormous value. Rival noble houses compete within a feudal society spread across planets. The novel won the first Nebula Award for Best Novel in 1966 and shared the Hugo, beginning the larger Dune Chronicles.

main.title: Highway 61 Revisited
main.summary: Bob Dylan released Highway 61 Revisited on 30 August 1965, continuing his move from acoustic folk towards rock accompaniment.

cards.heading: Highway 61 Revisited
cards.text: Bob Dylan released Highway 61 Revisited on 30 August 1965, continuing his move from acoustic folk towards rock accompaniment. Driving, blues-based music supports lyrics associated with the political and cultural atmosphere of contemporary America. Like a Rolling Stone preceded the album; Ballad of a Thin Man and the title track became enduring parts of his repertoire. The closing Desolation Row stretches to eleven minutes with a different musical setting. The title invokes the highway linking Dylan's Minnesota birthplace with southern centres of American musical history.

main.title: Moore's law
main.summary: Moore's law is the observation that the number of transistors in an integrated circuit (IC) doubles about every two years, with minimal increase in cost.

cards.heading: Moore's law
cards.text:
Moore's law is the observation that the number of transistors in an integrated circuit (IC) doubles about every two years, with minimal increase in cost. Despite the name, Moore's law describes an empirical relationship, not a scientific law. This type of observation, an experience curve effect, quantifies efficiency gains from learned experience in production.

The observation is named after Gordon Moore, the co-founder of Fairchild Semiconductor and Intel and former Chief Executive Officer of the latter, who in 1965 noted that the number of components per integrated circuit had been doubling every year, and projected that this rate of growth would continue for at least another decade. In 1975, looking forward to the next decade, he revised the forecast to doubling every two years, a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 41%. Moore's empirical evidence did not imply that the historical trend would continue; nevertheless, his prediction has held since 1975 and has since become known as a law.

main.title: Olivetti presents the Programma 101
main.summary: Olivetti presented the Programma 101 at the BEMA office-machine exhibition in New York in October 1965. Designed by Pier Giorgio Perotto's team, the programmable desktop calculator brought computing tasks onto a single desk.

cards.heading: Olivetti presents the Programma 101
cards.text:
Olivetti presented the Programma 101 at the BEMA office-machine exhibition in New York in October 1965. Designed by Pier Giorgio Perotto's team, the programmable desktop calculator brought computing tasks onto a single desk.

The Olivetti Programma 101, also known as Perottina or P101, is one of the first "all in one" commercial desktop programmable calculators.

Produced by Italian manufacturer Olivetti, based in Ivrea, Piedmont, and invented by the Italian engineer Pier Giorgio Perotto, the P101 used many features of large computers of that period. Volume production began in 1965. A futuristic design for its time, the Programma 101 was priced at $3,200 (equivalent to $32,700 in 2025).

main.title: Voting Rights Act
main.summary: Signed on August 6, 1965, the Voting Rights Act prohibited racial discrimination in voting and strengthened federal enforcement.

cards.heading: Voting Rights Act
cards.text: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 is a landmark U.S. federal statute that prohibits racial discrimination in voting. It was signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson during the height of the civil rights movement on August 6, 1965. Congress later amended the act five times to expand its protections. Designed to enforce voting rights protected by the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments to the United States Constitution, the act sought to secure the right to vote for racial minorities throughout the country, especially in the South. According to the U.S. Department of Justice, the act is considered to be the most effective piece of federal civil rights legislation ever enacted. The National Archives and Records Administration stated: "The Voting Rights Act of 1965 was the most significant statutory change in the relationship between the federal and state governments in the area of voting since the Reconstruction period after the Civil War".

main.title: Persona
main.summary: Persona is a 1966 Swedish psychological drama film written, directed, and produced by Ingmar Bergman and starring Bibi Andersson and Liv Ullmann.

cards.heading: Persona
cards.text:
Persona is a 1966 Swedish psychological drama film written, directed, and produced by Ingmar Bergman and starring Bibi Andersson and Liv Ullmann. The story revolves around a young nurse named Alma (Andersson) and her patient, well-known stage actress Elisabet Vogler (Ullmann), who has suddenly stopped speaking. They move to a cottage, where Alma cares for Elisabet, confides in her, and begins having trouble distinguishing herself from her patient.

Characterized by elements of psychological drama, Persona has been the subject of much critical analysis, interpretation, and debate. The avant-garde film's exploration of duality, insanity, and personal identity has been interpreted as reflecting the Jungian theory of persona and dealing with issues related to filmmaking, vampirism, homosexuality, motherhood, abortion, and other subjects. The experimental style of its prologue, storytelling, and end has also been noted. The enigmatic film has been called the Mount Everest of cinematic analysis; according to film historian Peter Cowie, "Everything one says about Persona may be contradicted; the opposite will also be true".

main.title: Revolver
main.summary: Revolver is the seventh studio album by the English rock band the Beatles.

cards.heading: Revolver
cards.text:
Revolver is the seventh studio album by the English rock band the Beatles. It was released on 5 August 1966, accompanied by the double A-side single "Eleanor Rigby" and "Yellow Submarine". The album was the Beatles' final recording project before their retirement as live performers and marked the group's most overt use of studio technology to date, building on the advances of their late 1965 release Rubber Soul. It has since become regarded as one of the greatest and most innovative albums in the history of popular music, with recognition centred on its range of musical styles, diverse sounds and lyrical content.

The Beatles recorded Revolver after taking a three-month break at the start of 1966, and during a period when London was feted as the era's cultural capital. Regarded by some commentators as the start of the group's psychedelic period, the songs reflect their interest in the drug LSD, Eastern philosophy and the avant-garde while addressing themes such as death and transcendence of material concerns.

main.title: Star Trek: The Original Series
main.summary: Gene Roddenberry's Star Trek began broadcasting in September 1966, following the USS Enterprise and its crew through the Milky Way.

cards.heading: Star Trek: The Original Series
cards.text: Gene Roddenberry's Star Trek began broadcasting in September 1966, following the USS Enterprise and its crew through the Milky Way. Captain James T. Kirk, science officer Spock and doctor Leonard McCoy lead its adventures in a twenty-third-century setting. William Shatner, Leonard Nimoy and DeForest Kelley play the central trio. The series ran for three seasons and seventy-nine episodes before NBC cancelled it in 1969 following low ratings. Those voyages began the franchise, with the original programme later distinguished as Star Trek: The Original Series.

main.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
main.summary: The Beatles released Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band in Britain on 26 May 1967, combining studio experimentation with an imagined band's identity.

cards.heading: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
cards.text: The Beatles released Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band in Britain on 26 May 1967, after ending their touring career the previous year. Paul McCartney's idea of an Edwardian military band supplied the album's central conceit. Studio production, songwriting and sleeve design worked together to extend the possibilities of a pop album. Its sound and imagery became closely associated with the era's youth culture and psychedelia. Critics praised the way it connected popular music with broader artistic ambitions, making the album itself an object of sustained attention.
